PullRequest.Title: Separate cloud sandbox provisioning, resume, and recovery telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Description

Distinguish provisioning a new cloud sandbox, reopening an existing environment, automatic connection recovery, and user-local host attachment without changing connection behavior or retry policy.

- Add `environmentOperation` and end-to-end `readinessMs` to `cloudSandboxConnectionOutcome`. Successful provisioning and resume samples both end at authenticated AHP readiness, so protocol waits after credential issuance remain included in the appropriate workflow.
- Record `provisioningMs` from task creation through connection start, and partition the existing connection duration into exclusive `preparationMs` and `connectionMs`. When the start time is known, `readinessMs = provisioningMs + preparationMs + connectionMs`.
- Emit a separate `cloudSandboxProvisioningOutcome` for API-phase creation success, failure, or cancellation, including failures before connection tracking starts.
- Keep provisioning timestamps local and out of persisted data; do not reuse them for recoveries or later independent dials. Missing creation timestamps produce absent readiness measurements, not zero provisioning time.
- Add regression coverage and document scorecard boundaries and comparison guidance.

`resume` describes opening an existing environment, including already-warm environments; it does not establish a cold VM resume. Pure server startup timing still requires a server-reported signal. Compare successful `readinessMs` samples by `environmentOperation`, rather than comparing API-only provisioning duration with full resume latency.

Only the ten source, test, and telemetry documentation diffs are included. No log files or session artifacts are included.

## How to test

Validation completed for these changes before moving the branch onto the latest `main` (five non-overlapping upstream commits):

- **Passed:** `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- **Passed:** `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run typecheck-client`
- **Passed, 240 tests:**
  ```sh
  node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxTelemetry.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts \
    --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.ts \
    --reporter dot
  ```
- **Passed, 14 tests:**
  ```sh
  node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium \
    --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts \
    --grep 'CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution provisioning' \
    --reporter dot
  ```
- **Passed after updating the branch:** `git diff --check`

Coverage includes long protocol waits, successful/failed/cancelled outcomes, credential retry backoff, missing provisioning metadata, user-local attachments, subsequent recovery/redial, and the task-creation timestamp handoff.

Runner limitation: the combined Chromium invocation stalled during loading, and Electron could not load the larger service/contribution test modules. The separate Chromium invocations above passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provision a new cloud sandbox and connect it through authenticated AHP readiness
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Account lookup, one task-creation request, local provider seeding/persistence, credential mint/wake, relay and protocol readiness must complete. The diff adds Date.now arithmetic, passes one numeric timestamp, and synchronously enqueues one two-field provisioning telemetry event; it does not await additional work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the sandbox task with POST /tasks; on specific unusable/error responses an existing best-effort DELETE may run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One POST per provisioning attempt; at most one cleanup DELETE on the existing failure paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create request, response parsing, and conditional cleanup ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The POST and response validation are required before connection; cleanup remains on the failure path. The new wrapper does not add or repeat either request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mint credentials/wake the environment and establish relay/protocol connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical credential flow and one logical connection flow per cold provisioning attempt, with existing internal retry policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provisioning already connected through the same credential and relay/protocol paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations remain the readiness critical path; the diff only supplies telemetry context and records phase durations around them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue cloudSandboxProvisioningOutcome with outcome and durationMs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one two-scalar event per createSession attempt, including failures and cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No separate provisioning outcome event was emitted; existing request and connection telemetry remained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call occurs immediately before resolving or rethrowing but has no await and constant payload size; it does not alter network request cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical provisioning attempt per user-created sandbox. Connection telemetry remains one tracker per environment address and diagnostic work scales with the bounded connection-stage events, not sessions, frames, or repository items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A provisioning call performs one create flow and one connection flow. Existing address-keyed connection tracking/reuse prevents duplicate trackers for the same live address; the diff adds no limiter, queue, fan-out, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. Existing live-connection reuse returns before creating telemetry, while a cold new environment creates one tracker. The timestamp is carried only on the first create-to-connect handoff and is not persisted or reused on later dials.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: call sites, address-keyed ownership, and boundary counts are explicit in the changed code and surrounding service flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry backend enqueue cost is implementation-dependent, but the payload and frequency are strictly bounded to one tiny event per explicit provisioning attempt.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly added work is O(1) per explicit provisioning attempt, with no added remote call, blocking await, collection fan-out, or retained growing state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resume an existing managed sandbox or attach to a user-local Mission Control host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing configuration checks, optional user-local identity/account checks and disconnects, credential minting, and relay/protocol readiness must complete. Added operation classification and duration partitioning execute inline as constant arithmetic and telemetry fields.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check the current local Agent Host environment for user-local attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one optional local-host query per user-local attach.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local-host query occurred before telemetry classification was added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for user-local safety; unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve account where required, mint credentials/wake, and connect through relay/protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical flow for the selected address, subject to existing retries and waking responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same account, credential, and connection boundaries ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains the connection critical path. The diff adds no request and only passes environmentKind into tracker creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing connection outcome with additional scalar operation and duration fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per logical connect outcome; event frequency is unchanged and payload growth is fixed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One connection outcome event was already emitted, with fewer scalar fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant synchronous event construction at terminal completion; no await or collection serialization is added.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected environment/address per resume. For user-local attachment, the pre-existing loop scales with currently attached local environments for the account; the diff neither creates nor enlarges that loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing address reuse returns immediately for a live connection. Otherwise one connection is established for the selected address; no new parallel boundary work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm live connections still bypass tracker creation. Cold resumes create one address-keyed tracker; subsequent independent dials deliberately create a fresh tracker without retaining provisioning provenance.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: tracker creation, live-address reuse, and terminal event emission are explicit and covered across resume and attach contexts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact telemetry serialization cost is not measured, but fixed payload growth cannot scale with environment history, repository size, or frame volume.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Fixed per-connect metadata does not change expensive-boundary count, effective concurrency, or cache behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatically recover a previously ready sandbox connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a disconnect, existing recovery credential and relay/protocol work must finish before readiness. The diff initializes two scalar counters, toggles preparation timing on bounded diagnostics, and adds fixed fields to the existing terminal outcome.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh/mint credentials as needed and reconnect relay/protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical recovery operation per observed disconnect, with existing retry behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Recovery already performed the same credential and transport/protocol operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged recovery critical path; added timing observes existing phase events only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing recovery connection outcome with fixed additional scalar measurements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per terminal logical recovery; no event-frequency increase.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same terminal recovery event was emitted with fewer scalar properties.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant event construction after recovery reaches a terminal state, without added await.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with logical recovery attempts and bounded phase transitions under the existing retry policy, not with received frames or connection lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Recovery remains owned by the existing per-address remote connection sequence. The diff does not introduce parallel recoveries, retries, or a new scheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Existing staged credentials and address-keyed telemetry ownership are retained and released on failed/disposed terminal states; provisioning timestamps are explicitly excluded from recovery operations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: recovery operation creation and cleanup are visible in onConnectionStateChange, and no changed boundary invocation exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Diagnostic event frequency depends on retry outcomes, but each existing diagnostic now incurs only constant Date.now/arithmetic work and active phases are bounded by the fixed phase enum.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff observes existing recovery work without increasing retries, remote calls, retained state, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provisioning fails or is cancelled before connection tracking begins
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The create request, response/body validation, and any existing cleanup must settle before the caller receives failure or cancellation. A single small provisioning telemetry event is enqueued immediately before rethrow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Task creation and conditional best-effort task deletion on unusable responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create request and at most one existing cleanup request per attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same failure and cancellation paths executed and rethrew without a provisioning outcome event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both boundary operations predate the diff; telemetry is emitted only after they settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue one failed or cancelled provisioning telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one constant-size event per terminal create attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No provisioning-specific terminal telemetry event was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous call before rethrow, but no await and only two scalar values.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One event per failed/cancelled createSession call; no collection or history-dependent work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No scheduling change. Each create call reports its own terminal outcome after existing request/cleanup behavior completes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or written by the new reporting wrapper, and failures are not retained for retry or negative caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: both success and catch paths call the reporter once, and the wrapper performs no retries or allocations proportional to input.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The local enqueue latency is not measured, but frequency is tied to explicit create attempts and payload size is fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only new terminal-path cost is one bounded telemetry enqueue.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. Traced provisioning, resume/attach, recovery, and pre-connection failure/cancellation paths, including network, IPC, cleanup, telemetry serialization, cache/reuse, and concurrency behavior. No actionable performance regression was introduced; all new work is bounded scalar bookkeeping or one constant-size event per existing logical operation.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
